If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) in the last 3 days, reduce forecast by 1.5–2.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to avoid overconfidence bias.  
If sentiment is consistently negative (≤-0.33) in the last 3 days, increase forecast by 1.5–2.5% for mid horizon (8–15 days) to counteract pessimism.  
If sentiment swings sharply from positive to negative within 3 days, apply a 2–3% downward correction to forecast at day 10–14 to align with sentiment reversal.  
For late horizon (16–30 days), if sentiment remains neutral (0.33–0.67), apply a 0.5–1.0% upward adjustment to compensate for lagging model inertia.  
If sentiment is positive but forecast shows a steep downward slope, reduce forecast by 1–2% at day 15–20 to prevent overcorrection.  
If sentiment is negative but forecast shows a steep upward slope, increase forecast by 1–2% at day 15–20 to prevent overoptimism.
